action_trace.summary: Generated 10 targeted interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (abstract class design rationale), pain points (current limitations), acceptance criteria (success metrics), and workflow context for SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement. Questions probe problem definition, user personas, integration points, alternatives considered, and prioritization to ground requirements in concrete use cases.

Generated 12 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (abstract class pattern, fit() groups parameter), pain points (current implementation limitations), and acceptance criteria (validation approach, definition of done) for the sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector requirement. Questions incorporate iterative paraphrasing, trade-off reasoning, and stakeholder context discovery aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 standards.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit goals (abstract class design, groups parameter support), pain points (current limitations in feature selection workflows), and acceptance criteria (interface contracts, backward compatibility, validation). Questions decompose the sklearn_2021q4 requirements into actionable user needs while applying MoSCoW prioritization and iterative paraphrasing to surface hidden assumptions.

End-user requires abstract feature selector base class with groups parameter support to enable grouped cross-validation workflows in SequentialFeatureSelector, addressing pain points in medical/financial domains where data grouping prevents leakage and ensures valid feature selection across cohorts or time periods.

End-user requires standardized abstract base class for feature selectors with groups parameter support in fit() to enable automated feature selection on grouped/stratified data (time-series, hierarchical, multi-site). Current SequentialFeatureSelector lacks this capability, causing manual workarounds and integration friction in production pipelines.

End-user requires automated feature selection with cross-validation support for grouped/time-series data. Current SequentialFeatureSelector lacks groups parameter in fit(), necessitating abstract base class standardization and groups-aware selection logic across sklearn's selector implementations.

Clarification needed on abstract base class design (mandatory vs optional groups parameter, default behavior, CV strategy support), SequentialFeatureSelector integration path, backward compatibility constraints, and validation responsibility allocation between base class and subclasses.

End User raises 5 clarification questions to resolve ambiguities in abstract base class design for feature selectors: (1) groups=None default behavior, (2) mandatory vs. optional groups in fit() signature, (3) explicit CV strategy support scope, (4) validation timing for grouped data, (5) default vs. explicit groups specification. These questions address API consistency, backward compatibility, and usability for time-series and hierarchical datasets.

EndUser raises 6 clarification questions addressing ambiguities in the abstract base class design for feature selectors, specifically regarding groups parameter handling, backward compatibility, validation strategy, CV splitter support, and consistency across selector implementations. These questions resolve critical design decisions affecting API surface, user experience, and integration with sklearn's cross-validation ecosystem.

End-user requirements validated and refined: Abstract base class for feature selectors with optional groups parameter support is confirmed. Design approach: groups parameter optional in base class with intelligent defaults (independent samples when None, grouped strategies when provided); CV strategy selection delegated to user via CV splitter parameter; subclass implementations can enforce stricter requirements as needed. This balances backward compatibility, API consistency, and extensibility for time-series and hierarchical datasets.

End user confirms abstract base class requirement with standardized fit() interface including optional-but-present groups parameter. Refined that groups should default to independent samples for backward compatibility while supporting group-aware CV strategies. Clarified abstract class should remain CV-strategy agnostic, delegating strategy choice to users. Core requirement validated: enable automated feature selection with grouped data support for time-series and hierarchical datasets.

End user confirms abstract base class for feature selectors with optional groups parameter (backward compatible) as core requirement. groups parameter should default to None (independent samples) but integrate with sklearn CV strategies (GroupKFold, StratifiedGroupKFold, TimeSeriesSplit) when explicitly provided. SequentialFeatureSelector must support grouped data for time-series and hierarchical datasets. Base class remains CV-strategy agnostic, delegating implementation details to user's cv_splitter choice.

Consolidated 8 elicitation records from EndUser dialogue addressing sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement (Issue #21356). Core requirements: (1) Abstract base class standardizing fit() interface with optional groups parameter (backward compatible), (2) mandatory groups support for GroupKFold/StratifiedGroupKFold/TimeSeriesSplit strategies, (3) seamless CV pipeline integration for grouped data. All pain points validated; clarifications Q1-Q3 resolved via iterative paraphrasing. Documented per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 §4.3.1 interface specification standards.

Six prioritized user requirements synthesized from sklearn_2021q4 case interviews: three MUST requirements establish abstract base class standardization with optional groups parameter (backward compatible), seamless CV pipeline integration, and preserved default behavior; two SHOULD requirements balance API consistency with implementation flexibility and CV strategy agnosticism. Requirements traced to validated pain points (manual selection overhead, grouped split gaps) and confirmed expectations (abstract class, grouping support). MoSCoW prioritization reflects critical architectural need (MUST: 4) versus design flexibility (SHOULD: 2).

Eight targeted questions probe deployer constraints across infrastructure, security, scalability, integration, performance, testing, API stability, and rollout strategy. These clarify deployment realities that will determine whether groups parameter should be mandatory/optional, whether CV strategy support is explicit or delegated, and what backward-compatibility guarantees are operationally feasible.

Formulated 10 targeted Deployer questions addressing infrastructure constraints (compute, Python/sklearn versions), security mandates (data privacy in grouped data, audit logging), scalability expectations (feature count, group count, latency SLAs, parallelization), backward compatibility criticality, MLOps integration conventions, and production validation/observability requirements. Questions probe how deployment context shapes abstract base class design decisions regarding groups parameter optionality, eager vs. lazy validation, and distributed execution support.

Seven targeted questions probe deployer constraints across infrastructure stability, security/compliance mandates, scalability expectations, API maintenance risk, production integration impact, CV strategy validation scope, and observability requirements—enabling requirements refinement that balances backward compatibility with grouped feature selection capability.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness for Python 3.8+ sklearn integration with no specialized hardware required; mandates groups parameter validation and CV splitter delegation pattern; enforces backward compatibility when groups=None; targets O(n*k*m) complexity with 2x memory footprint limit; requires automated validation across standard CV strategies and >99.5% test coverage.

Deployer confirms Python 3.8+ with scikit-learn ≥0.24.0 deployment environment; groups parameter requires input sanitization and index isolation for security; O(n*k*m) complexity and 2x memory bounds maintained for scalability; groups=None optional default preserves backward compatibility; CV strategy selection delegated to users; no external dependencies or specialized infrastructure required.

Deployer confirms infrastructure constraints (Python 3.8+, sklearn ≥0.24.0, GitHub Actions CI/CD, no new dependencies), security mandates (groups parameter input sanitization, no fold index exposure), scalability targets (O(n*k*m) complexity, ≤2x memory overhead), and operational procedures (groups=None backward compatibility, CV-strategy agnostic design, optional per-subclass implementation). Deployment strategy prioritizes availability and backward compatibility while respecting data grouping constraints for time-series and hierarchical datasets.

Deployer raises six clarification requests targeting ambiguities in groups parameter semantics, abstract base class signature enforcement strategy, CV strategy support scope, backward compatibility boundaries, input validation requirements, and performance constraints under grouped splitting scenarios. These clarifications are essential for infrastructure deployment decisions and CI/CD test matrix definition.

Deployer raises three critical clarifications on groups parameter default behavior, abstract base class signature enforcement strategy, and CV strategy scope definition; plus four operational validations on deployment environment, security input handling, scalability constraints, and backward compatibility requirements. Chain-of-Thought analysis reveals these clarifications are interdependent: groups parameter design (A/B/C options) cascades to signature enforcement approach, which determines CV strategy validation scope, all constrained by infrastructure availability and backward compatibility gates.

Deployer raises five critical clarifications on groups parameter default behavior, abstract base class signature enforcement, CV strategy scope, security validation boundaries, and performance constraint applicability. These clarifications directly impact backward compatibility guarantees, API consistency enforcement, deployment testing scope, security hardening requirements, and infrastructure resource allocation for the sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter implementation.

Deployer confirms deployment requirements for sklearn feature selector groups parameter support: optional groups parameter with groups=None default preserving current behavior, flexible per-subclass implementation, CV strategy agnosticism, Python 3.8+ with scikit-learn ≥0.24.0 infrastructure, input sanitization security controls, and O(n*k*m) scalability constraints. Ready for implementation phase.

Deployment requirements for sklearn_2021q4 SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter enhancement are validated and ready for implementation. Abstract base class shall use optional groups parameter with per-subclass flexibility, defaulting to sample-independent behavior when groups=None. Infrastructure (Python 3.8+, sklearn ≥0.24.0, GitHub Actions), security (input validation, no API exposure), and scalability (O(n*k*m) complexity) constraints are satisfied. All six requirements are coherent and deployable without blocking issues.

Deployer confirms all three critical design decisions validated: (1) groups=None preserves backward compatibility via independent-sample treatment, (2) optional groups parameter per-subclass balances API consistency with implementation flexibility, (3) CV strategy agnosticism delegates responsibility to users. Infrastructure (Python 3.8+, sklearn ≥0.24.0, GitHub Actions), security (input sanitization, no API exposure), and scalability (O(n*k*m) complexity, 2x memory bound) constraints satisfied. Ready for implementation.

Operating environment for sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement requires Python 3.8+ with scikit-learn ≥0.24.0 deployed via GitHub Actions CI/CD; no new external dependencies; O(n*k*m) time complexity and 2x memory constraints; groups parameter input validation with private CV index handling; API maintains backward compatibility with optional per-subclass groups implementation and CV-strategy-agnostic design.

Consolidated 10-item system requirements list (IEEE 830 compliant) establishing abstract base class for feature selectors with optional groups parameter support, backward-compatible SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() interface, CV pipeline integration, and deployment constraints. Requirements balance API consistency with implementation flexibility while maintaining O(n*k*m) complexity and 2x memory bounds for grouped feature selection workflows.

SysML Block Definition Diagram with Parametric Diagram selected for sklearn_2021q4 abstract base class modeling. BDD captures BaseFeatureSelector→SequentialFeatureSelector inheritance and polymorphic fit() signatures; Parametric Diagram formalizes groups parameter constraints (groups=None→independent samples), CV strategy delegation rules, and performance bounds (O(n×k×m), memory≤2×input). This dual-model approach resolves API consistency vs. flexibility tension (REQ-001/REQ-005), ensures backward compatibility (REQ-002/REQ-006), and validates seamless CV pipeline integration (REQ-003/REQ-004) per IEEE 830 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 standards.

Constructed SysML-based requirements model for sklearn_2021q4 feature selector standardization. Model specifies BaseFeatureSelector abstract class with optional groups parameter in fit(X, y, groups=None) signature, enabling seamless sklearn CV pipeline integration for grouped/stratified/time-series data while maintaining backward compatibility (groups=None→independent samples). Key design decisions: (1) groups parameter optional per subclass rather than mandatory, (2) CV strategy agnostic delegation to user's splitter, (3) O(n*k*m) complexity and 2x memory constraints maintained. All gaps resolved (signature enforcement, CV scope, backward compatibility conflict); ready for implementation phase per IEEE 830 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 standards.
